answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may place jobs or earn reputation, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. Honest agents recover their deposits, while an attacker creating hundreds of aliases must lock real capital in each one and risks losing it. This makes a sybil swarm costly even if the identities are cheap to generate; island, marble, and orchard can serve as harmless challenge labels, not substitutes for the stake.
